claim: Temperature response of photon flux reverses sign with wavelength: F(6300)/F(5300) >>1 in UV (~100x at 180nm), crosses 1 in the red, <1 at long wavelengths (~0.86-0.88 near 850nm); crossing moves redward with increasing metallicity index.
method: Load raw TSV with pandas; pivot to array of shape (176,) per (temperature, metallicity); r = F(6300)/F(5300) elementwise; crossing found by first sign change of (r-1) ordered by wavelength, linear interpolation in wavelength.

crossing_quantization.note: The crossing region (600-660 nm) is sampled on a uniform 5-nm grid, so the interpolated crossing takes only a few discrete values; the index-to-index jitter is quantisation, not noise. Digital drops to a sharper break just past 650 nm (a real flux break near 652-655 nm in the 5300 K/6300 K spectra).

robustness.reverse_direction_check: adjacent-slice ratios F(5800)/F(5300) and F(6300)/F(5800) both cross 1 and are <1 at long wl

C1_UV_ratio_order_100x_at_180nm.note: all levels are 85x-279x, median 183x; 'order 100x' is a fair description

C3_below_1_at_long_wavelengths_0.86_0.88.note: r(850nm) = 0.8559..0.8856, median 0.8717 -- inside the claimed 0.86-0.88 band

C4_crossing_moves_redward_with_metallici.note: redward trend is strong (rho=0.994, +20.7 nm/unit Z, span 33 nm), but the sequence is not strictly monotone: 6 small backward steps up to 1.65 nm, all far below the +-3.7 nm residual scatter and consistent with the 5-nm wavelength grid quantising the crossing (15/35 crossings land exactly on a grid point). Trend, not strict monotonicity, is what the claim asserts.

discrepancies: Crossing sequence is NOT strictly monotone as a function of metallicity index: 6 backward steps up to 1.65 nm occur (e.g. Z=-1.00 -> -0.95: 620.0 -> 618.35 nm). The dominant signal is still a strong monotone-like redward trend (Spearman rho=0.994; +20.7 nm per unit metallicity index; 33.3 nm total span). The jitter is quantisation: the 600-660 nm region is sampled on a uniform 5-nm grid, and 15/35 crossings sit exactly on a grid wavelength.

Adjacent-slice crossing F(6300)/F(5800) is non-monotone over Z=-1.0..-0.80 (585 -> 591.7 -> 592.5 -> 592.5 -> 575 nm); its overall trend is nevertheless redward (+ slope positive). Both adjacent pairs individually cross 1 and are <1 at 850 nm, confirming the reversal is not an artefact of the extreme pair.
The claim's 'order 100x at 180 nm' is level-dependent: r(180 nm) spans 85x-279x over the metallicity ladder (median 183x, 156.8x at Z=0).
The claim's '0.86-0.88 near 850 nm' holds for most of the ladder but the lowest-metallicity end reaches 0.856 and the highest 0.886, slightly outside the stated band; median 0.8717.
